They overruled #8A5A33 with #6B4226 for contrast, which is a fair call. They rejected one-per-5s in favour of two per loop for a felt beat, and that reason mostly holds.

j-rosie-tran.note: Refused with a reason: a drip stroke outside the cup reads as a second subject, so the team enlarged the held scar instead. The reason is fair, but the hole still looks like a dot to me.

j-amara-diallo.note: Slip, ghost and hard cuts all deleted and the drop now fades in and squash-fades out; code matches the pitch.

j-mara-okafor.note: The orange pips, slip and ghost are all gone, as asked. I asked for the drop and ring to be the only clock; they refused because 'a cup with no count is a glide'. That reason does not hold: the 1s drop already counts, and the new count resets just as visibly as the pips did.

j-rosie-tran.note: Landed and then some: they removed the orange band and ghost at every size, not only at 120px, and kept the one-second drop and the five-step count, now in crema.

The stream ends at the spiral's origin (54,57), which orbits the 54,60 pivot by 3 units, so you can barely see it move.

j-rosie-tran.note: Idea taken but geometry changed: they made a static stream from the top edge to the pivot, always visible, not a line to a moving tip. It helps the pour read, but the spiral still turns.

j-sun-park.note: Layer split refused as a point of gain for a second SVG and a stacking bug surface; honest and README-disclosed, and the reason is defensible, but the repaint cost is unchanged.

signature_awards.description: Whether a tired, low-vision user can name 'coffee in progress' from one frozen frame at 120px, through grayscale and a 1.5x blur, with a deliberate reduced-motion cue and a specific accessible name.
signature_awards.why: Light cup on dark, spout and falling drop read as coffee even in blurred grayscale, the crema steps are a real progress cue, and the aria-label names the order; early dark crema steps are low contrast.

signature_awards.description: Pause at 0s, 1.25s, 2.5s, 3.75s and the worst frame I can scrub to, print each in one ink at 2cm on kraft, and ask whether every still is a composed, ownable mark that belongs to one family.
signature_awards.why: Every sampled still is the same top-down cup with an off-centre dark mark in a different size and place, a stamp family that survives one ink; the bare-field frames at 0s and 2.5s are plain but not broken.

signature_awards.description: At every moment exactly one element carries 'working on it', and every other moving part is visibly quieter, nearby, and on a tempo that nests with the lead rather than competing with it.
signature_awards.why: One dark hole at a time is the clear lead; the 5s field bloom and the 2.5s glint nest under it, and the reduced-motion version keeps a single breathing scar as the focal point. The two drops land about 11 units apart, which nudges the eye slightly.

signature_awards.description: Scores whether the loader already shows coffee being made in the first frame a customer sees after tapping order, at 120px, with no beat needed to start the motion.
signature_awards.why: The stream and the spiral are both in place at frame one, so a restart reads as the pour carrying on.

signature_awards.description: How much of the loader repaints per frame, how many layers it promotes, and whether it costs nothing when idle or hidden.
signature_awards.why: Six shapes, fills only, zero JS in the path, will-change only on the two scars; but SVG-child animation still repaints the whole 120px each frame and there is no play-state hook.

criteria.name: Coffee concept & ownability
criteria.description: One clear idea drawn from the ritual of coffee (grind, bloom, pour, crema, tamp, drip) rather than generic steam-over-a-cup; it could belong to this one café-ordering brand and could anchor a wider motion language.

criteria.name: Motion, timing & perceived wait
criteria.description: Purposeful timing, rhythm and easing that make the wait feel shorter and calmer; the 5s cycle loops seamlessly and reads as steady, ongoing progress, never as stalled or as a finish that then resets.

criteria.name: Engineering craft & performance
criteria.description: Lean, self-contained build that honours every technical constraint: compositor-friendly animation (transform/opacity), crisp scaling from 120px to full splash, no jank on weak devices, readable and maintainable code.

criteria.name: Glanceability & inclusion
criteria.description: A half-awake customer understands 'your coffee is on its way' in one second at 120px; nothing flashes or demands attention; the prefers-reduced-motion version still clearly says 'working on it'.

criteria.name: Pitch
criteria.description: Short, persuasive, honest about trade-offs and risks; explains the idea, the timing choices, and why it would hold up across real wait times.

lessons.lesson: Strong loaders keep a coffee subject and a progress cue visible in every frozen frame and under blur, and say so in a specific accessible name; weak ones only work while you watch them move.
In coffee, the strong work puts the motion inside the drink and makes every still printable on a sleeve; the weak work bolts a UI gesture (a spin, a fill, a counter) onto a cup and calls it ritual.
The strong loaders are the ones where one thing moves and everything else breathes; the weak ones keep a second idea (a counter, a hitch, a reset) that the waiting eye has to track.
Strong coffee loaders show coffee moving into the cup from the first frame, in a shape a half-awake eye reads at 120px; weak ones show a dot or a turning rosette.

Strong loaders keep the moving part small, on its own layer, and driven by nothing but a pausable CSS clock; weak ones animate five things inside one SVG and call it lean because the keyframes only touch transform and opacity.
